<!-- cli-reference:start — generated by `go run ./tools/sitecli` from the CLI; edit the command's help in the code, not this block -->

Ingest test signals (JUnit/lcov) the project generated and bind them to the map.

```text
Consumes the test runner's artifacts and writes the signals into the map:

  anchors ingest --junit results.xml      execution: which tests passed/failed
  anchors ingest --lcov coverage.info     line coverage per code file
  anchors ingest --mutation mutation.json  mutation: does the test PROVE the line, or only run it?
  anchors ingest --mutation m.json --scope isolated   the unit's test only
  anchors ingest --mutation m.json --scope full       with the dependents' tests
  anchors ingest --junit r.xml --lcov c.info   several in one pass

Anchors does NOT run the test — you run it (jest --coverage, go test -coverprofile,
pytest-cov…) and hand over the report. From the execution, Anchors also derives coverage per
SCENARIO: a scenario code (SPCRX-V01) is PROVEN if it appears in a case that passed.
Run 'anchors coverage' afterwards to see the spec requirements with no green test.
```

## Usage

```bash
anchors ingest [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--junit` |  | JUnit XML file (execution result) |
| `--layer` |  | test layer of this suite (unit\|integration\|e2e…); default unit — merges several |
| `--lcov` |  | lcov .info file (line coverage) |
| `--logs` |  | scan the logs declared in `logs.paths` and bind the failure occurrences to the specs that declare them |
| `--map` |  | path to the map |
| `--mutation` |  | mutation JSON report. The FORMAT belongs to the project: declare it in the mutation-score gate of anchors.yaml, key 'format' (default 'mutation-testing-elements' — Stryker/PIT/Infection/mutmut; 'gremlins' for Go) |
| `--partial` |  | the report is a PARTIAL run (only some tests): scenarios it did not run keep their earlier proof. `anchors test --changed` sets it |
| `--root` | `.` | project root |
| `--scope` |  | scope of the suite that ran the mutants: `isolated` (only the unit's test) or `full` (with the dependents). Ingesting both allows reading the DIFFERENCE — how much the unit depends on third parties to prove itself |
| `--suite` |  | name of this suite in the map (default: the JUnit path relative to the root). Proofs are kept per suite, so each workspace's report only speaks for itself |

## The map and its signals — family

Commands of the same family — what tells each apart:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`anchors map`](/docs/cli/commands/map/) | Operate the dependency map (anchors.graph.yaml) |
| **`anchors ingest`** | Ingest test signals (JUnit/lcov) the project generated and bind them to the map |
| [`anchors test`](/docs/cli/commands/test/) | Run the test suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| [`anchors mutation`](/docs/cli/commands/mutation/) | Run the mutation suites declared in anchors.yaml and ingest the reports |
| [`anchors keep-evidence`](/docs/cli/commands/keep-evidence/) | Declare that a change proves nothing new, keeping the files' evidence fresh |
| [`anchors stamp`](/docs/cli/commands/stamp/) | Write the missing `@contract` stamps on test doubles (never rewrites an existing one) |
| [`anchors recode`](/docs/cli/commands/recode/) | Rename an identity code and propagate it across the project |
| [`anchors renumber`](/docs/cli/commands/renumber/) | Renumber the revisions this branch added when the base already took their number |
| [`anchors generated-paths`](/docs/cli/commands/generated-paths/) | The paths of DERIVED files — whoever conflicts in them rebuilds |
| [`anchors merge-progress`](/docs/cli/commands/merge-progress/) | Progress merge driver: unites both sides, `[x]` beats `[ ]` |
